name: Efficiency
definition: At GitLab, efficiency means producing results without wasting materials, time, or energy. We optimize solutions globally for the broader GitLab community over one person or a small group. Focus on efficiency should be global in nature, not just local to a given function.

rows.situation: When the interesting solution and the boring one both work
rows.under: Picks the novel one, because it is more satisfying to build.
rows.justRight: Picks the boring solution. Novelty is a cost paid by everyone who maintains it.
rows.over: Refuses a genuinely better new approach because it is unfamiliar.

rows.situation: When the efficient thing for your team is costly elsewhere
rows.under: Optimizes locally. The cost lands on another function and nobody counts it.
rows.justRight: Optimizes globally for the broader community, even when your own function gets slower.
rows.over: Models the global picture so exhaustively that the local decision never gets made.

rows.situation: When you are asked something for the third time
rows.under: Answers again in a direct message, and the answer stays private.
rows.justRight: Puts the answer in the handbook, and sends the link. Write it once, use it many times.
rows.over: Sends a link instead of an answer when the person needed judgment, not documentation.

rows.situation: When a meeting is being scheduled
rows.under: Accepts it, and the decision waits a week for a calendar slot.
rows.justRight: Handles it asynchronously in writing, and keeps meetings for what genuinely needs them.
rows.over: Refuses every synchronous conversation, and a 10-minute misunderstanding takes four days.

rows.situation: When the consistent process is slower
rows.under: Follows the process because it is the process.
rows.justRight: Asks what the consistency buys. Keeps it where it compounds and drops it where it only tidies.
rows.over: Abandons shared process so often that everyone pays to relearn how things are done.

rows.situation: When the work could be polished further
rows.under: Ships something that does not do the job, and calls it efficient.
rows.justRight: Spends the energy where it changes the outcome, and stops when the next hour buys nothing.
rows.over: Optimizes a process that runs twice a year and will never repay the effort.
